Claude Sonnet 5.5 Cache Read Price Cut · AI Signal

 By Álvaro Lucero Rufino October 13, 2026 pricing anthropic prompt-caching 

# Claude Sonnet 5.5 Cache Reads Fall to $0.10: The Bill Math

 Source Anthropic platform release notes (October 7, 2026) and pricing page, read on October 13, 2026 ↗ 

On October 7, 2026 Anthropic halved one price of Claude Sonnet 5.5: reading a prompt from the cache now costs $0.10 per million tokens instead of $0.20. Nothing else moved. This post checks the change against Anthropic’s own pages, read again on October 13, 2026, puts it next to the cache prices of the models around it, and works out what it does to the monthly bill of one cached workload at three hit rates. The release notes give no reason for the change, and this post does not guess one.

## What Anthropic changed, in its own words

The platform release notes entry for October 7, 2026 reads: “We’ve lowered the price of prompt cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from $0.20 USD to $0.10 USD per million tokens: 0.05x the base input price instead of 0.1x. Cache writes and all other prices are unchanged.”

Anthropic’s pricing page, read on October 13, 2026, prints the row as `Claude Sonnet 5.5 | The best combination of speed and intelligence | $2 / MTok | $10 / MTok | $2.50 / MTok | $4 / MTok | $0.10 / MTok` (input, output, 5-minute cache write, 1-hour cache write, cache read). Its caching table now names the model in the exception: “Cache read (hit) | 0.1x base input price (0.025x on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1; 0.05x on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5)”. This site recorded the change on its price-changes page as a decrease by the provider, effective October 7, 2026, after reading the new figure on October 11. All five figures on the page match the dataset row, verified on October 12.

| Claude Sonnet 5.5, per 1M tokens | Until October 6, 2026 | From October 7, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | $2.00 | $2.00 |
| Output | $10.00 | $10.00 |
| Cache write, 5 minutes | $2.50 | $2.50 |
| Cache write, 1 hour | $4.00 | $4.00 |
| Cache read | $0.20 | $0.10 |

## Next to the other Claude models

The models a Sonnet 5.5 user is most likely to weigh it against, with the prices on Anthropic’s page on October 13, 2026:

| Model | Status in this dataset | Input | Cache read | Cache read as share of input |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | current | $0.10 | $0.01 | 0.1x |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | current | $2.00 | $0.10 | 0.05x |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | current | $4.00 | $0.20 | 0.05x |
| Claude Sonnet 4.6 | current | $3.00 | $0.30 | 0.1x |
| Claude Sonnet 4.5 | deprecated, retires November 30, 2026 | $3.00 | $0.30 | 0.1x |

Haiku 5.5’s figures are its list for prompts up to 100,000 tokens; above that line every one of its prices is five times higher, as our post on its threshold works through. Claude Sonnet 5, which Anthropic now lists under “Additional models”, still prints $0.20 for cache reads with the same $2, $10, $2.50 and $4 as Sonnet 5.5, so since October 7 the two differ on that one line only.

Sonnet 5.5 came out after our cache price survey of September 16, which found a cache hit at 10% of the input price to be the norm. It launched at that norm, $0.20 on $2, and since October 7 sits below it, with Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1.

## What the cache-write rule adds

A cache read is only half of the arithmetic. The pricing page’s caching table lists “5-minute cache write | 1.25x base input price | Cache valid for 5 minutes” and “1-hour cache write | 2x base input price | Cache valid for 1 hour”, and explains when each is charged: “Cache write tokens are charged when content is first stored. Cache read tokens are charged when a subsequent request retrieves the cached content.” The October 7 change touched neither write price, so on Sonnet 5.5 a 5-minute write still costs $2.50 per million tokens, 25 times the new read price.

# Claude Sonnet 5.5 cache reads cost half: measure your own savings - DEV Community

Author: Dave Kurian
Published: 2026-10-09T03:13:00Z
Source: dev.to
Language: en

## Story

Claude Sonnet 5.5 cache reads cost half: measure your own savings - DEV Community

Dave Kurian

 Posted on Oct 9 • Originally published at otf-kit.dev 

# Claude Sonnet 5.5 cache reads cost half: measure your own savings 

Anthropic cut the Claude Sonnet 5.5 prompt-cache read rate on October 7, 2026, from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens. The change halves the price of a cache read, but it does not halve an application’s model bill. Your impact depends on how many cache-read tokens your traffic actually generates, how much new caching writes cost, and how often requests miss.

Start with the usage counters your application already receives. Compare the same workload before and after the rate change, and keep the calculation separate from output tokens, uncached input, retries, and any other price changes. That gives you a defensible read-cost delta without turning a vendor price cut into an unmeasured savings claim.

## What changed on October 7 

Anthropic’s release notes say Sonnet 5.5 cache reads moved from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens. The note also says cache writes and all other prices are unchanged. The new read rate is $0.10 per million tokens; the old rate was $0.20.

The direct difference is therefore $0.10 for each million cache-read tokens, assuming the same token volume and billing terms. This is a change to one line of usage. It is not a claim that your total Anthropic spend falls by 50 percent: output generation, uncached input, cache creation, request volume, retries, and other models remain separate parts of the bill.

For an existing workload, first calculate the counterfactual on the cache reads you actually recorded:

`read_cost_delta = cache_read_tokens / 1,000,000 × ($0.20 - $0.10)`

For example, if a hypothetical month contains 25 million Sonnet 5.5 cache-read tokens, that same read volume cost $5 at the former rate and $2.50 at the new rate. The $2.50 difference is arithmetic from the published rates, not a forecast for your application. Use your own counters and invoice to establish your result.

## Find the calls that can benefit 

The change matters most to a route that already gets cache hits on a substantial, repeated prefix. Examples include a stable system instruction, shared reference material, or tool definitions reused across requests. The important evidence is not how large a prompt looks in a source file. It is how many of its tokens are reported as cache reads after the request runs.

Do not add caching solely because reads are cheaper now. A first request can create cached content, and cache writes are unchanged by this price change. A prompt that changes on every call may create writes without earning enough later reads to offset them. Put stable content before request-specific data, and measure whether the exact route is reusing that prefix.

Start by grouping traffic by model ID and operation: for example, support classification, code review, or a repository assistant’s repeated project context. Keep the grouping stable across the comparison. If you combine Sonnet 5.5 with other models, or combine unrelated request types, a workload shift can look like a price effect.

## Log reads, writes, and ordinary tokens separately 

The response usage object distinguishes cache reads from cache creation and ordinary input. Persist those counters with the model ID, route, timestamp, request outcome, and an internal request class. Avoid storing customer prompts or secrets just to calculate billing. Aggregated counters are enough for the price comparison.

A small helper can calculate the read line and the rate-change delta from one response:

  cache_read_input_tokens?: number;
  cache_creation_input_tokens?: number;
  input_tokens: number;
  output_tokens: number;
};

Claude API Pricing 2026: All Models, Cache, and Batch

# Claude API Pricing (2026)

This page lists Anthropic's current Claude API prices, explains the two discount mechanisms that change your effective rate, and covers a tokenizer detail that makes Claude bills differ across model generations even at the same list price.

## Claude model prices

List prices verified 2026-10-11. USD per 1 million tokens, standard tier.

| Model | Input $/1M | Cache read $/1M | Output $/1M | Context | Max output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Fable 5.1 | $10.00 | $0.25 | $50.00 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | $4.00 | $0.20 | $20.00 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | $2.00 | $0.10 | $10.00 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 (up to 100K prompt) | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.50 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 (over 100K prompt) | $0.50 | $0.05 | $2.50 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Fable 5 (legacy) | $10.00 | $1.00 | $50.00 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Opus 5 (legacy) | $5.00 | $0.50 | $25.00 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Opus 4.8 (legacy) | $5.00 | $0.50 | $25.00 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Sonnet 5 (legacy) | $2.00 | $0.20 | $10.00 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Sonnet 4.6 (legacy) | $3.00 | $0.30 | $15.00 | 1,000,000 | 128,000 |
| Claude Haiku 4.5 (legacy) | $1.00 | $0.10 | $5.00 | 200,000 | 64,000 |

Claude Sonnet 5 launched with $2.00 input / $10.00 output as introductory pricing. Anthropic has made that its standard price, and the planned move to $3.00 / $15.00 will not happen. Claude Haiku 5.5 bills $0.50 input / $2.50 output for the whole request once the prompt passes 100,000 tokens, with cache reads and writes counted toward that length.

## Prompt cache pricing

Prompt caching changes the input rate on repeated content. The mechanics:

- Cache reads bill at 0.1x the input price on most models, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, and 0.025x on Fable 5.1. On Sonnet 5.5 that is $0.10 per 1M tokens instead of $2.00.
- Cache writes bill at 1.25x the input price for the 5-minute TTL, or 2x for the 1-hour TTL.

The write premium is small next to the read discount. Content that gets written once and read many times, a system prompt, tool definitions, a document under discussion, costs 90% to 97.5% less on every read after the first request, depending on the model. For agent and coding workloads where the same prefix repeats on every step, cached reads become most of the input bill.

## Batch API: 50% off

The Batch API applies a 50% discount to both input and output. It suits any job that does not need an immediate response, such as bulk classification, evaluation runs, and offline content generation.

## The tokenizer difference between generations

Claude has no public tokenizer. Exact counts come from the free count_tokens API. That matters here because the tokenizer differs by model generation. Opus 4.7 and later, including every 5.x model, use a newer tokenizer that produces roughly 1x to 1.35x the tokens of the 4.6-and-older family on the same text. Sonnet 5 counts about 30% more tokens than Sonnet 4.6 for identical text.

So the same prompt can bill differently across Claude generations for two separate reasons: the price per token, and the number of tokens the prompt becomes. Sonnet 5 lists at $2.00 per 1M input tokens against $3.00 on Sonnet 4.6, but the same text counts as about 30% more tokens on Sonnet 5, so the real saving is smaller than the list prices suggest. When you compare Claude models, count the prompt with the count_tokens API for each model rather than assuming one count.

Anthropic Slashes Claude Sonnet 5.5 Cache-Read Cost by 50% – Unite.AI - TradePoint.io

# Anthropic Slashes Claude Sonnet 5.5 Cache-Read Cost by 50% – Unite.AI

 October 7, 2026 in AI & Technology Reading Time: 4 mins read 

Anthropic on October 7, 2026, lowered the price of cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 by 50%, from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens, effective immediately. The company also introduced a monthly Claude Platform API credit for Max and Team subscribers: $100 per month for Max 5x, $200 per month for Max 20x, and up to $500 per month pooled across users on Team plans.

Both changes were announced alongside the launch of Claude Haiku 5.5, the company’s new small model, in the “Further updates” section of the Claude Haiku 5.5 announcement. Anthropic described the moves as improvements to the value of its models and products.

## Sonnet 5.5 Cache-Read Pricing

The reduction applies to cache reads, the tokens billed when a subsequent API request retrieves previously cached content. Cache reads on Sonnet 5.5 now cost $0.10 per million tokens rather than $0.20. Because cache reads make up a large share of models’ token consumption, Anthropic said, the change reduces the cost of running Sonnet 5.5 on most agentic tasks by around 20%. The company illustrated the shift with a Terminal-Bench 4.0 chart plotting Sonnet 5.5’s accuracy against cost per attempt at both the old and new cache-read rates.

The prompt-caching section of Anthropic’s Claude Platform pricing documentation states that a cache hit now costs 5% of the standard input price on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5: $0.20 per million tokens on Opus 5.5 and $0.10 on Sonnet 5.5. The documentation lists a 2.5% rate on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 and the standard 10% rate on all other models. Under its multiplier system, five-minute cache writes are billed at 1.25 times the base input price and one-hour writes at twice the base input price. Sonnet 5.5’s remaining rates are unchanged: $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, $2.50 per million tokens for five-minute cache writes, and $4 per million tokens for one-hour cache writes.

Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5.5 on September 28, 2026, pricing it the same as Sonnet 5 at $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, and $0.20 per million tokens for cache reads. The new rate replaces that launch cache-read price while leaving the rest of the model’s pricing intact.

## Monthly API Credits by Plan

The second change adds a recurring monthly credit for the Claude Platform, Anthropic’s API environment. Anthropic said the credit is designed to let subscribers experiment with building tools, apps, and agents that call its API, and that it can be used on any of the company’s models. Per the program’s Help Center terms, Max 5x subscribers receive $100 per month and Max 20x subscribers receive $200 per month. On Team plans, credits accrue per seat ($20 per Standard seat and $100 per Premium seat) and pool into a single monthly balance capped at $500. Discounted Team plans, including Nonprofit and Scientists plans, receive the same per-seat amounts. Anthropic’s worked example gives a team with three Standard seats and two Premium seats $260 a month, and states that adding another Premium seat would raise the next cycle’s credits to $360. The pool is calculated from the seats on the plan each time credits are deposited.

Free, Pro, and Enterprise plans are not eligible. A Max or Team subscription must be active and in good standing, and new subscribers can claim once they have been on an eligible plan for seven days. Subscriptions can be purchased on the web, iOS, or Android, but credits are claimed on claude.ai in a web browser, with no payment method required on the Claude Platform. Anthropic’s official developer channel announced the rollout on October 7, 2026, stating that the credits work on any model, including Haiku 5.5, in customers’ own code or third-party harnesses.

results.text:
# Anthropic halved Sonnet 5.5 cache reads, and its own tool showed the old price for two days

Author: Shane S. Ellison
Published: 2026-10-11T18:09:27Z
Source: mixed-news.com
Language: en

## Story

Anthropic halved Sonnet 5.5 cache reads, and its own tool showed the old price for two days
# Anthropic halved Sonnet 5.5 cache reads, and its own tool showed the old price for two days
Oct 11 2026 Shane S. Ellison
Anthropic halved the price of prompt cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 on October 7, and for the next two days its own coding tool priced them at the old rate. The cut is in Anthropic's platform release notes: "We've lowered the price of prompt cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from $0.20 USD to $0.10 USD per million tokens: 0.05x the base input price instead of 0.1x. Cache writes and all other prices are unchanged."
The Claude Opus 5.5 launch card, with the model name in white over a photograph of a horizon at dusk. Image: Anthropic
Claude Code caught up on October 9. The changelog entry for version 2.1.296 reads: "Updated **/cost**, the status line, **--max-budget-usd** and the SDK's cost figures to price Sonnet 5.5 cache reads at $0.10 per million tokens (was $0.20)." So four places where Claude Code puts a price on a session were each working to a figure Anthropic had stopped charging.
## What the cut is worth on a cached prompt
A cache read is what you pay to reuse a prompt prefix you have already stored, and it is the bulk of the token traffic in any agent that keeps reloading the same instructions and the same files. Anthropic's pricing page now lists Claude Sonnet 5.5 at $2 per million input tokens, $2.50 for a five-minute cache write, $4 for a one-hour write, $0.10 for a cache read and $10 per million output tokens. A footnote carries the multiplier: "Cache hits and refreshes on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are priced at 0.05x the base input price."
Every other current Claude model stays on the standard 0.1x, with Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 at 0.025x. Claude Opus 5.5 did not move either: its base input price is $4, so 0.05x of that is the $0.20 per million tokens the page still gives it. One model got cheaper to re-read, and it is the one Anthropic launched in late September at $2 and $10 per million tokens.
## Two days of figures at twice the rate
The dates are first-party on both halves. Anthropic dates the price change to October 7 in its release notes. Version 2.1.295 of Claude Code went to the npm registry at 18:22:58 UTC on October 8 without the correction, and 2.1.296 followed at 16:58:10 UTC on October 9 with it. Anywhere in that window, **/cost** and the status line were reporting cache reads at $0.20 per million tokens against a billed rate of $0.10.
Anthropic does not say that anyone was billed the old rate, and the wording is careful: what changed in 2.1.296 is the cost figures the tool displays. On a cache-heavy session, the displayed figure for those tokens would have been double the rate Anthropic had published.
## Why an Anthropic date is not quite a date
One caveat belongs on any figure quoted from these pages. Anthropic edits release-note entries after publishing them, including the text under earlier date headings, so an entry dated October 7 is what the page said at the moment it was read rather than a record of what shipped that day. Everything quoted here was read at 21:33 to 21:35 UTC on October 10, and the npm publication times at 21:52 UTC the same day.
The separate stable release channel is on 2.1.287, published on October 1, and by the changelog's own account any build before 2.1.296 prices Sonnet 5.5 cache reads at the old $0.20. Anthropic has shipped these releases quickly all month, fast enough for 2.1.293 to withdraw a cloud-session fix two days after shipping it. For anyone reading a running total, the version printing it is part of the figure.

## Story

Claude Sonnet 5.5 halves cache-read prices. Migration can still change your bill | OpenTools

Updated 9 minutes ago

Source: Anthropic pricing and migration guide; Artificial Analysis. Figure: OpenTools Team. Original figure using factual source data. · Source image

# Claude Sonnet 5.5 halves cache-read prices. Migration can still change your bill

Input and output token prices match Sonnet 5, while cache reads now cost half as much. Effort defaults, thinking behavior and unsupported API settings still make migration more consequential than a model‑ID swap.

Input and output stayed flat; cache reads did not

Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5 on September 28 with the same base input and output prices as Sonnet 5: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Anthropic's current pricing table lists a real discount elsewhere: cache reads cost $0.10 per million tokens on Sonnet 5.5, half Sonnet 5's $0.20 rate. Neither change is evidence that the same uncached workload will produce the same bill.

Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 generates output more than 30% faster and costs up to 30% less per task because it often uses fewer tokens to finish work. Those are workload‑level claims from the model maker, not a cut to the $2/$10 base rates. An independent launch evaluation from Artificial Analysis found the opposite at the maximum effort setting: roughly 193,000 output tokens and $7.60 per Intelligence Index task, about 50% more than Sonnet 5 in that suite. The evaluator described it as the highest output‑token use it had measured.

Both findings can be true. A lower or middle effort setting can finish many well‑scoped tasks efficiently, while the maximum setting spends far more tokens pursuing a higher score. Anthropic's own launch charts make the same general point: cost and score move with effort, and Sonnet 5.5 complements Opus most clearly at lower settings. Teams should treat “up to 30% less” as a hypothesis to test on a pinned workload, not as a new base input/output price.

Medium and High are different starting lines

The default effort depends on where the model is used. In Claude apps and Claude Code, Sonnet 5.5 defaults to Medium. On the Claude Platform API, it defaults to High. Anthropic recommends Medium for well‑specified agentic tasks and High for harder or longer work, while latency‑sensitive chat may start at Medium or Low.

That split can distort a casual evaluation. A developer who compares the app with an API integration without pinning effort may be comparing two reasoning budgets as well as two interfaces. A production migration that simply swaps the model name and accepts the API default can also change latency and token use even when the prompt stays identical.

The safer sequence is to freeze the task set, set `output_config.effort` explicitly and run at least two plausible levels. Record strict task completion, output tokens, wall‑clock latency, retries and human repair time. The public Claude Sonnet 5.5 model page is a useful place to compare its stable model facts; use Anthropic's current pricing table for cache‑read rates, and test the launch‑specific decision on the organization's own workload and chosen effort.

Several old request patterns now return errors

Anthropic's migration guide lists changes that can turn a model swap into a 400 error. Sonnet 5's `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` is not supported. To keep up‑front thinking off, Sonnet 5.5 uses `between_tools`, and only at Low, Medium or High effort. Xhigh and Max require adaptive thinking. `between_tools` also prevents changing effort in the middle of a conversation.

Forced tool choice changes too. Requests that use a tool choice of `any` or a named `tool` are rejected. Anthropic directs Claude API users to `auto` with strict tool schema

results.text:
Why is Claude so expensive? The token math · SSD Nodes

 Guides By Matt Connor 2026-10-11 

# Why is Claude so expensive? The token math

Output tokens cost five times input, and every turn re-reads your whole context. See the arithmetic on one real session, and the four levers that cut it.

## Why is Claude expensive? The short answer

Claude is expensive for four reasons that stack on top of each other. Output tokens are priced at five times the rate of input tokens. The API keeps no memory of your conversation, so the whole history is sent again and billed again on every turn. An agent turns one question into dozens of API calls, and each call carries that growing history. On top of all that, the frontier model is priced against the difficulty of the work it does, not against the cost of running a small model.

A token is a piece of text. As a rough guide, one token is about four characters, or about 0.75 words of English. Rates are quoted per million tokens, written MTok (million tokens). Every rate below is the published Claude API rate as of October 2026.

Most surprise bills come from the second and third reasons on that list. People usually arrive believing the answers Claude writes are what costs money. In an agent session, the writing is often less than one tenth of the bill.

## The published rates, so we agree on the numbers

Chart Published Claude API rates, US dollars per million tokens, October 2026

| label | input_usd | output_usd | cache_read_usd |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Haiku 4.5 | 1 | 5 | 0.10 |
| Sonnet 5 | 2 | 10 | 0.20 |
| Sonnet 4.6 | 3 | 15 | 0.30 |
| Opus 5 | 5 | 25 | 0.50 |

The data behind this chart

```
[
  {
    "label": "Haiku 4.5",
    "input_usd": 1,
    "output_usd": 5,
    "cache_read_usd": "0.10"
  },
  {
    "label": "Sonnet 5",
    "input_usd": 2,
    "output_usd": 10,
    "cache_read_usd": "0.20"
  },
  {
    "label": "Sonnet 4.6",
    "input_usd": 3,
    "output_usd": 15,
    "cache_read_usd": "0.30"
  },
  {
    "label": "Opus 5",
    "input_usd": 5,
    "output_usd": 25,
    "cache_read_usd": "0.50"
  }
]
```

Look at the shape rather than the absolute numbers. Every model charges exactly five times more for output than for input. Opus 5 costs 5 dollars per million input tokens and 25 dollars per million output tokens. Haiku 4.5 costs 1 and 5. So the distance from the cheapest model in this table to the most expensive one is five times, and the distance from reading to writing is also five times.

Sonnet 5 costs 2 and 10 dollars per million. Anthropic first sold that price as an introductory rate through August 31, 2026, then made it the standard price and cancelled the planned rise to 3 and 15 dollars. Rates move with model releases, so check the current ones before you build a budget on them. Newer models keep the same five times shape: Opus 5.5 lists at 4 and 20 dollars per million, Sonnet 5.5 at 2 and 10, and Haiku 5.5, released October 7, 2026, from 0.10 and 0.50. There is no free tier sitting below this table either, though new accounts start with a small credit and some parts of the API cost nothing at all.

The last column is the cache read rate. It decides most bills. Come back to it after the arithmetic.

## Why do output tokens cost five times input tokens?

Reading and writing are not the same amount of work. Input tokens are processed in one pass. The model reads the whole prompt at once and the work runs in parallel across it, which is why a 60,000 token prompt does not take 60,000 times longer to read than a 1,000 token prompt.

Output tokens are produced one at a time. Each new token needs its own pass through the model, and it needs every token before it as context. Writing 1,000 tokens means 1,000 passes, one after another. That serial work cannot be spread out the way reading can, so each output token holds the hardware for longer.

This is why "make the answer shorter" is a weaker lever than people expect. It works on the smaller half of an agent bill.

## Why
